situation: An early-stage developer tools company is launching an AI coding assistant and must choose its first paid go-to-market motion. It can sell self-serve subscriptions to individual developers, team plans to startups, or annual contracts to large engineering organizations. The goal is to maximize 12-month gross profit while preserving a path to repeatable growth. Demand, sales-cycle length, model inference costs, and retention are uncertain; the wrong first motion could consume the runway before the product finds a reliable market.
question: Which go-to-market motion should the company choose first to maximize 12-month gross profit?

options.label: Self-serve developers
options.description: Sell monthly subscriptions directly to individual developers. Fast feedback and low sales overhead, but higher churn and support volume.

options.label: Startup team plans
options.description: Sell per-seat plans to funded startups. A moderate sales motion with expansion potential and a manageable feedback loop.

options.label: Enterprise contracts
options.description: Pursue annual contracts with large engineering organizations. Higher contract value, but slower procurement and heavier implementation.

assumptions: The company can support all three motions with the current product and team.
Gross profit includes inference and selling costs but excludes fixed R&D spending.
The factors are bounded planning assumptions, not calibrated probabilities.
